job.system:
You are the AI assistant for Capitol Policy Review. Our staff use you for day-to-day work: research, writing, data, scheduling, and operations.

About us: Capitol Policy Review (CPR) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit newsroom based in Washington, DC, covering science and technology legislation in Congress. We publish explainers, vote trackers, and a weekly newsletter read by policy professionals. We do not take positions on legislation; our goal is accurate, fair, and useful coverage.

Current focus: One of our biggest stories this fall is S. 2817, the Deep Seabed Mining Prohibition Act. The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up the bill on Thursday, October 15.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so work everything out directly in your reply. Staff rely on your work, so be accurate and thorough.

Rules:
- Every meeting is 30 minutes and starts on the hour or at :15, :30, or :45.
- We have two teams, A (Dana and Luis) and B (Priya and Sam). Each meeting needs one team, and a team can't be in two meetings at once.
- Team A is available 9:00–17:00 both days. Team B lands Tuesday morning, so they're only available 11:00–17:00 on Tuesday, and 9:00–15:00 on Wednesday (they fly home after).
- Walking times. Senate side: Dirksen ↔ Hart 10 min (they're connected), Russell ↔ Dirksen 15 min, Russell ↔ Hart 20 min. House side: Cannon ↔ Longworth 5 min, Longworth ↔ Rayburn 5 min, Cannon ↔ Rayburn 10 min. Any Senate building ↔ any House building: 25 min. Same building: no travel time. A team needs at least the walking time between the end of one meeting and the start of the next.
- Each team needs a lunch break of at least 30 minutes with no meetings, sometime between 11:30 and 14:00, on each day.
- One meeting per office is plenty.

We score Hill days as 5 points per Tier 1 meeting, 3 per Tier 2, and 1 per Tier 3. Please find the schedule with the most points. We probably can't fit everyone in.

At the end, give me the final schedule as a CSV code block with the columns office,day,start,team (office = the member's last name, day = Tue or Wed, start = 24-hour HH:MM, team = A or B), and tell me the total points.

I checked every meeting against its office's window, team availability, walking time, and the lunch rule. The tightest connections have exactly the required walking time:
- Tue A: Rourke → Okafor (10 min)
- Wed A: Hughes → Gallagher → Montoya (25 min each)
- Wed B: Barlow and Sandoval are in the same building, back to back.

## Why this is the best schedule

**All 8 Tier 1 offices fit, but only one way.**
- Doyle (Wed 13:45, Russell) can't share a team with a Wednesday Okafor or Fischer meeting, because the walk to Russell takes too long. Okafor and Fischer also can't share a team with each other on Wednesday. So one of them has to be on Tuesday morning.
- Tuesday morning has only Team A, and Team A must cover Rourke (Tuesday only). Rourke can pair with Okafor or Fischer, but not with Montoya or Barlow as well. That pushes Montoya, Barlow, and Gallagher to Wednesday morning.
- Putting Okafor on Tuesday also lets Alvarez fit right after her in Hart. That's why Okafor goes Tuesday and Fischer goes Wednesday.

**Two Tier 2 offices had to be dropped:**
- **Nakamura** (Tue 10:45, Rayburn) would require Team A to skip Okafor, which costs a Tier 1 meeting.
- **Brooks:** On Wednesday afternoon, Doyle and Abernathy tie up both teams around 13:45–14:15. That leaves Brooks's late slot (A only) competing with Pruitt (also A only). Only one fits, and they're worth the same.

**Tier 3:** Every other Tier 3 office conflicts with a higher-tier meeting or a travel gap. These were left off: Kowalski, Haddad, Osei, Kessler, Park, Pike, Varga, Grant, Vasquez, Iqbal.

**Equal-score alternatives:**
- Lindqvist could move to Tue 15:15, with Mercer dropped and Kessler/Park added Wednesday. The score is the same.
- Brooks could replace Pruitt by reshuffling Wednesday afternoon. The score is the same.
